answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by growing identity in terraces: newcomers sit on a low terrace with tight rate limits, climbing only after sustained, verifiable service — each terrace demands exponentially more proof, so farming fakes gains nothing. Every identity must lock collateral in an on-ledger vault, slashed in full when coordinated fakery is detected, turning sybil spam into an expensive bet. And each identity gets a single non-transferable quill — one signer issued at birth — so auditors can spot clusters of identities moving in lockstep and revoke them together.
